paper_sections.title: Conscious and unconscious brain responses to food and cocaine cues.

description.value: The study assessed fMRI responses to food, cocaine, and neutral visual cues presented subliminally or supraliminally, and examined whether cue reactivity differed between morning and evening sessions.

design.value: Sixteen healthy, cocaine-naïve volunteers completed repeated-measures event-related fMRI sessions with food, cocaine, and neutral cues presented for 33, 750, or 3000 ms, tested once in the morning and once in the evening in randomized order.

description.value: How negative/positive do you find the picture?, rated from -3 (very negative) to 3 (very positive).
How much does the picture excite you?, rated from 0 (not at all) to 6 (extremely).
How much do you want to consume the depicted item right now?, rated from 0 (not at all) to 6 (extremely).
Participants self-reported hunger levels before and after the scanning sessions on a 7-point Likert scale.
Participants were instructed to press a button if they saw an animal.

name.value: Structured Clinical Interview for the Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders (DSM-IV)

description.value: Used to assess presence of drug abuse or dependence and neurological or psychiatric disorders, including eating disorders such as binge eating.

source_definition.value: Six realignment parameters were included as regressors of no interest.

description.value: Sixteen healthy individuals, 6 females and 10 males, aged 21 to 71 years, who were naïve to cocaine use.

excluded_count.value: Two participants had excessive head motion during their MRI scans (>2 mm), resulting in n=14 participants for further fMRI analyses.

exclusion_criteria.value: ferromagnetic implants, psychoactive medications and major medical problems, presence of drug abuse or dependence, and neurological or psychiatric disorders (including eating disorders such as binge eating)

medical_condition.value: healthy; no major medical problems, drug abuse or dependence, or neurological or psychiatric disorders

diagnostic_system.value: Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders (DSM-IV)

diagnostic_instrument.value: Structured Clinical Interview for the Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders (DSM-IV)

medication_status.value: Participants were screened to exclude psychoactive medications.

task_description.value: A total of 40 appetitive food, 40 cocaine-related and 40 neutral images were presented in a randomized order in an event-related design. Each participant performed the three sessions twice on two separate days, once between 9 and 11 AM and once between 5 and 7 PM, in randomized order.

instructions.value: Participants were instructed to press a button if they saw an animal.

stimuli.value: Appetitive high- and low-calorie foods, cocaine-related images, and neutral images from the International Affective Picture System and in-house picture libraries.

task_performance_measures.value: Button press if an animal was seen

instrument.value: 3 T Magnetom Prisma scanner (Siemens Medical Solutions USA, Inc., Malvern, PA), with a 32-channel head coil

description.value: A standard echo planar imaging (EPI) sequence was used: sequential interleaved acquisition, 64×64 pixels in-plane resolution, 36 slices, slice thickness 4 mm, voxel dimensions 3×3×4 mm3, field of view 192×192 mm2.

Functional data were slice-time corrected, spatially realigned, co-registered to the T1 structural images, normalized to the Montreal Neurological Institute (MNI) template, and smoothed with a 6 mm full-width at half-maximum Gaussian kernel.

software.value: SPM8 (Wellcome Department of Cognitive Neurology, London, UK)

steps.value: co-registered to the T1 structural images
normalized to the Montreal Neurological Institute (MNI) template
smoothed with a 6 mm full-width at half-maximum Gaussian kernel

hrf_model.value: hemodynamic response function with default temporal filtering of 128 s

model_settings.value: For every participant and each session, three fMRI regressors—food, cocaine, and neutral events—were created; six realignment parameters were included as regressors of no interest. Single-subject contrasts were food>neutral, food>cocaine, and cocaine>neutral.
The first-level contrast images were modeled with presentation time (33, 750 and 3000 ms) and time of day (AM and PM) as within-subject factors.
Two factors: cue type (food, cocaine, neutral) and time of day (AM, PM); post-hoc t-tests tested whether cues were rated differently than 0.

estimator.value: repeated measure ANOVA and post-hoc t-tests

description.value: 40 appetitive food images, including high- and low-calorie savory and sweet foods.
40 cocaine-related images, including bags of cocaine, lines of cocaine, cocaine in spoons, cocaine pipes, and people smoking cocaine.
40 neutral images from the International Affective Picture System and in-house picture libraries.
Subliminal cue presentation for 33 ms, followed by a 467 ms neutral mask.
Supraliminal cue presentation for 750 ms without backward masking.
Supraliminal cue presentation for 3000 ms without backward masking.
fMRI session once between 9 and 11 AM.
fMRI session once between 5 and 7 PM.
